script: Welcome to Chengyu Bites — your quick summary on Chinese 成语. Get ready to learn how artistry can capture life itself! [break 1s] The phrase is: 惟妙惟肖, wéi miào wéi xiào. [break 1s] 惟 (wéi) - only, just [break 0.5s] 妙 (miào) - wonderful, exquisite [break 0.5s] 惟 (wéi) - only, just [break 0.5s] 肖 (xiào) - to resemble, to be like [break 1s] So, the full idiom 惟妙惟肖 literally means 'only wonderful, only resembling,' and figuratively refers to something that is perfectly lifelike or vividly detailed. [break 1s] Here’s the story behind it: [break 1.5s] This idiom originally comes from the realm of art, specifically painting and sculpture. It is said that a talented artist could create a work so lifelike that it seems to come alive. The phrase emphasizes the skill involved in capturing the essence of a subject with remarkable detail. Over time, it evolved to describe anything that is strikingly vivid or realistic. [break 1.5s] Example 1: 他的画惟妙惟肖，仿佛可以说话。 [break 1s] His painting is so lifelike that it seems to speak. [break 1s] Example 2: 这个雕塑惟妙惟肖，令人惊叹。 [break 1s] This sculpture is so vivid that it astonishes everyone. [break 1s] Example 3: 她的表演惟妙惟肖，观众都入迷了。 [break 1s] Her performance was so captivatingly realistic that the audience was mesmerized. [break 1s] So, that’s 惟妙惟肖, which means perfectly lifelike. Thank you for tuning in! Thanks for listening to Chengyu Bites! See you next time for another idiom. [break 1s]
